question.leadin: Answer the following about anti-Black racism in the United States.
question.text: The death of this Florida teenager at the hands of George Zimmerman is often seen as a starting point for the Black Lives Matter movement.
question.clue: In 2012, another widely publicized shooting occurred when George Zimmerman shot this high school student wearing a hoodie and carrying Skittles.

swap.leadin: Answer the following questions about a candidate in the 2016 Republican primaries.
swap.text: In a rally supporting Trump, this Tea Party politician called her supporters "proud clingers," a phrase which briefly went viral after her speech.
swap.clue: During her term as governor, she dealt with the "bridge to nowhere" incident, and dismissed Walt Monegan, her public safety commissioner.

question.text: The Saturday Night Massacre was completed when Nixon made this third man the acting Attorney General and got him to fire Cox. In 1987, President Reagan nominated this man to the Supreme Court, but the Senate voted him down.
question.clue: William Saxbe replaced him as acting Attorney General, a position he took on after the resignation of William Ruckelshaus.

swap.leadin: Name the following about politicians who like getting hit in the face.
swap.text: In a charity boxing match, this 2012 Republican U.S. presidential candidate and former governor of Massachusetts lasted two rounds against Evander Holyfield.
swap.clue: This man once claimed he had "binders full of women" and that 47% of Americans would never vote for him.

question.leadin: Answer the following about recent natural disasters.
question.text: The northeastern United States was hit by this hurricane in October of 2012. Obama's relatively quick response to the devastation wrought by this hurricane may have boosted his election numbers in heavily affected states.

swap.leadin: This person announced her candidacy for a house seat in New Mexico in May 2019.
swap.text: Name this former CIA agent, who had her position leaked by Robert Novak after her husband, Joseph Wilson, investigated claims that Iraq had purchased uranium from Niger.

question.leadin: This election's eventual winner emerged victorious following the Supreme Court's overturning of a prior ruling requiring a recount in Florida.
question.text: Name this election decided following the Court's ruling in Bush v. Gore.
question.clue: One of those candidates pledged to put Medicare in a "lockbox" in this election, in which "hanging chads" and "butterfly ballots" may have resulted in Pat Buchanan getting extra votes.

swap.text: During his reelection campaign in 1984, Reagan's team aired this optimistic advertisement. It presented the ways that life had gotten better under Reagan's presidency, comparing the present to the title time of day.
swap.clue: The 1984 Reagan ad, "Prouder, Stronger, Better," which asks "Why would we ever want to return to where we were less than four short years ago?" is better known for opening with this line, which became his reelection slogan.

question.text: This New York mayor has been making budget cuts over his first eighteen months in office.
question.clue: In late 2008 he convened a special hearing of the city council to allow him to run for an unprecedented third term.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about presidential powers.
swap.text: This power, granted to the president in 1996 but ruled unconstitutional in 1998, allowed him to omit specific spending requirements from a budget bill without killing the bill in its entirety.
swap.clue: This power, by which the executive could disapprove some parts of a bill but leave others intact.

question.leadin: This judge wrote the majority opinion in Morse v. Frederick, which upheld a suspension from school for a student who displayed the banner "BONG HiTS 4 JESUS" outside of school.
question.text: Name this man who succeeded William Rehnquist in 2005 as Chief Justice.
question.clue: In one opinion, this Justice argued that an "individual mandate" should be seen as a tax, and is therefore constitutional.

swap.text: During the 1964 election, this conservative wrote the pro-Goldwater book A Choice, Not an Echo. This activist founded the Eagle Forum and was noted for her opposition to the Equal Rights Amendment.
swap.clue: This activist founded the Eagle Forum which grew out of a movement named STOP or "Stop Taking Our Privileges."

question.leadin: In May 2017 this man issued an apology to the Chobani Yogurt Company for his allegation that a plant of that company was involved in a child abuse ring and was responsible for rises in tuberculous cases.
question.text: Name this far right-wing radio host and conspiracy theorist, known for spreading his views through InfoWars.com. This man claims that Donald Trump personally called him the day after being elected to thank him for his campaign efforts.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about political scandals in the 1980s.
swap.text: This Senator from Colorado withdrew his campaign for the Democratic nomination shortly after photos were released of him and Donna Rice on a yacht named Monkey Business.
swap.clue: In his first campaign for his party's nomination, his opponent quoted a Wendy's commercial in asking him "Where's the beef?"

question.leadin: Answer the following about fiendish Republican strategist Lee Atwater.
question.text: This conservative columnist claimed Atwater requested he spread rumors about Dukakis. He is better known for partnering with Rowland Evans and for outing Valerie Plame as a CIA operative in 2003.

swap.text: Following the shooting, Milk's body was discovered by this politician who was then the president of the Board of Supervisors. This politician replaced Moscone as mayor, eventually being elected in her own right to two full terms.
swap.clue: When the CIA Torture Report was released, this Californian and oldest active Senator chaired the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence. Richard Burr replaced this Democrat as committee chairman in January 2015.

question.leadin: The first effort to sequester the federal budget was instituted by an act named for this senator, Warren Rudman, and Fritz Hollings.
question.text: Name this Texas senator, the first namesake of a 1999 act that overturned part of the Glass-Steagall Act, which he sponsored with Jim Leach and Thomas Bliley.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about writings on genocide and civil war.
swap.text: This woman wrote A Problem from Hell about American foreign policy on genocides in the 20th century. She was the U.S. Ambassador to the UN from 2013 to 2017.

question.text: Although viewed by conservatives as a right-wing vote, Souter voted with the majority in this case, which ruled that schools could not sponsor clerics in even non-denominational prayers. This case dealt with a rabbi delivering a prayer at a graduation ceremony.

swap.leadin: The winning candidate in this election made such bloopers as saying that Pearl Harbor occurred on September 7 and that he stood for "anti-Semitism." Answer the following about the election of 1988.
swap.text: Possibly the most exciting moment in the campaign occurred in the vice-presidential debates when this Dukakis running mate and Texas Senator sneered that Dan Quayle was "no Jack Kennedy."
swap.clue: He became president of Lincoln Consolidated during a fifteen-year absence from politics, which ended when he defeated George Bush in a 1970 election for senator from Texas.
